questions.question: Which of the following components of the AWS Global Infrastructure consists of one or more discrete data centers interconnected through low latency links?
questions.explanation: An Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers interconnected through low-latency links. Edge locations are for content caching, and a Region is a group of AZs.

questions.question: One benefit of On-Demand Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) pricing is:

options.text: The ability to bid for a lower hourly cost.
Paying a daily rate regardless of time used.
Pre-paying for instances and paying a lower hourly rate.

questions.explanation: With On-Demand EC2 pricing you pay only for the time used, with no upfront commitment. There is no bidding (that was the old Spot model), no flat daily rate, and no prepayment as with Reserved Instances.

questions.question: What can assist in evaluating an application for migration to the cloud? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Professional Services (B) and the AWS Partner Network (D) can help evaluate and plan an application's migration to the cloud. Trusted Advisor, Systems Manager, and Secrets Manager are not migration-assessment programs.

questions.question: A characteristic of edge locations is that they:

options.text: Host Amazon EC2 instances closer to users.
Help lower latency and improve performance for users.
Cache frequently changing data without reaching the origin server.

questions.explanation: Edge locations help lower latency and improve performance by serving cached content close to users. They do not host EC2 instances, cache constantly changing data without the origin, or refresh only daily.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways for a customer to interact with AWS services? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Customers interact with AWS services through the Command Line Interface (A) and the Software Development Kits (C) (and the console/API). On-premises, SaaS, and hybrid are deployment concepts, not interaction methods.

questions.question: What is a value proposition of the AWS Cloud?

options.text: AWS is responsible for security in the AWS Cloud.
AWS manages user applications in the AWS Cloud.

questions.explanation: A value proposition of the AWS Cloud is that no long-term contract is required — you pay as you go. AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (not in it), provisioning takes minutes (not days), and AWS does not manage your applications.

questions.question: A company is migrating an application that is running non-interruptible workloads for a three-year time frame. Which pricing construct would provide the MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: For non-interruptible workloads over a three-year term, Reserved Instances are the most cost-effective (largest committed-term discount). Spot can be interrupted, and On-Demand/Dedicated cost more for steady long-term use.

questions.question: Which AWS service is used to track record, and audit configuration changes made to AWS resources?
questions.explanation: AWS Config tracks, records, and audits configuration changes to AWS resources over time. Shield is DDoS protection, IAM is access, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which feature of the AWS Cloud will support an international company’s requirement for low latency to all of its customers?
questions.explanation: AWS's global reach (Regions and edge locations worldwide) supports low latency for an international company's customers. Fault tolerance, pricing, and high availability address other needs.

questions.question: How can one AWS account use Reserved Instances from another AWS account?

options.text: By using Amazon EC2 Dedicated Instances.
By using AWS Organizations consolidated billing.
By using the AWS Cost Explorer tool.

questions.explanation: Reserved Instance benefits are shared across accounts through AWS Organizations consolidated billing, so one account can benefit from another's RIs. Dedicated Instances, Cost Explorer, and Budgets do not share RIs.

questions.question: What are the benefits of developing and running a new application in the AWS Cloud compared to on-premises? (Select TWO)

options.text: AWS automatically distributes the data globally for higher durability.
AWS will take care of operating the application.
AWS makes it easy to architect for high availability.
AWS can easily accommodate application demand changes.
AWS takes care of application security patching.

questions.explanation: Building in the AWS Cloud makes it easy to architect for high availability (C) and to accommodate changing application demand (D). AWS does not operate your application, auto-distribute your data globally, or patch your application for you.

questions.question: Which of the following services falls under the responsibility of the customer to maintain operating system configuration, security patching, and networking?
questions.explanation: With Amazon EC2, the customer maintains the operating system configuration, security patching, and networking (e.g., security groups). RDS, ElastiCache, and Fargate are managed services where AWS handles more of this.

questions.question: AWS supports which of the following methods to add security to Identity and Access Management (IAM) users? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: You can add security to IAM users with Multi-Factor Authentication (D) and by enforcing password strength and expiration policies (E). Rekognition, Shield, and security groups are not IAM user security methods.

questions.question: Which service provides a hybrid storage service that enables on-premises applications to seamlessly use cloud storage?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is the hybrid storage service that lets on-premises applications seamlessly use AWS cloud storage. Glacier is archival, Snowball is physical transfer, and EBS is block storage.

questions.question: Where should a company go to search software listings from independent software vendors to find, test, buy and deploy software that runs on AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace is where you search ISV software listings to find, test, buy, and deploy software that runs on AWS. Artifact provides compliance docs, Lumberyard was a game engine, and CloudSearch is search.

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the AWS Global Infrastructure?
questions.explanation: AWS Regions are a component of the AWS global infrastructure. Alexa, Lightsail, and Organizations are services, not global-infrastructure components.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model adjusts based on supply and demand of EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances have prices that adjust based on the supply and demand of spare EC2 capacity. On-Demand and Reserved pricing do not fluctuate this way.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its applications to a VPC on AWS These applications will need to access on-premises resources. What combination of actions will enable the company to accomplish this goals? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use the AWS Service Catalog to identify a list of on-premises resources that can be migrated
Build a VPN connection between an on-premises device and a virtual private gateway in the new VPC
Use Amazon Athena to query data from the on-premises database servers
Connect the company’s on-premises data center to AWS using AWS Direct Connect
Leverage Amazon CloudFront to restrict access to static web content provided through the company’s on-premises web servers

questions.explanation: To let VPC applications reach on-premises resources, build a VPN connection to a virtual private gateway (B) and/or use AWS Direct Connect (D). Service Catalog, Athena, and CloudFront do not provide this connectivity.

questions.question: A Cloud Practitioner must determine if any security groups in an AWS account have been provisioned to allow unrestricted access for specific ports. What is the SIMPLEST way to do this?

options.text: Review the inbound rules for each security group in the Amazon EC2 management console to check for port 0.0.0.0/0.
Run AWS Trusted Advisor and review the findings.
Open the AWS IAM console and check the inbound rule filters for open access.
In AWS Config, create a custom rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to review firewall rules for inbound access.

questions.explanation: The simplest way to find security groups allowing unrestricted access is to run AWS Trusted Advisor and review its security findings. Manually checking each group, using the IAM console, or building a custom Config/Lambda rule are more effort.

questions.question: Which of the following security-related services does AWS offer? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS offers Trusted Advisor security checks (B) and data encryption (C) among its security-related services. AWS does not provide MFA physical tokens itself, automated pen testing, or S3 copyright detection.

questions.question: Which of the following services have Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) mitigation features? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS WAF (A) and Amazon CloudFront (D) include DDoS mitigation features (and integrate with AWS Shield). DynamoDB, EC2, and Inspector are not DDoS-mitigation services.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS features enables a user to launch a pre-configured Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance?
questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lets you launch a pre-configured EC2 instance. EBS is storage, Systems Manager is operations management, and AppStream streams applications.

questions.question: A solution that is able to support growth in users, traffic, or data size with no drop in performance aligns with which cloud architecture principle?
questions.explanation: Supporting growth in users, traffic, or data with no performance drop aligns with implementing elasticity (scaling with demand). Think parallel, decoupling, and design-for-failure address other goals.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud benefit eliminates the need for users to try estimating future infrastructure usage?

options.text: Easy and fast deployment of applications in multiple Regions around the world.
Lower variable costs due to massive economies of scale.

questions.explanation: The elasticity of the AWS Cloud eliminates the need to estimate future usage, since you scale up or down as demand changes. Multi-Region deployment, security, and economies of scale are separate benefits.

questions.question: What can users access from AWS Artifact?

options.text: A download of configuration management details for all AWS resources.
A security assessment of the applications deployed in the AWS Cloud.

questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides AWS security and compliance documents (reports, certifications, agreements). It does not provide configuration details, training materials, or application security assessments.

questions.question: Compared with costs in traditional and virtualized data centers, AWS has:

options.text: Greater variable costs and greater upfront costs.
Fixed usage costs and lower upfront costs.
Lower variable costs and greater upfront costs.
Lower variable costs and lower upfront costs.

questions.explanation: Compared with traditional and virtualized data centers, AWS has lower variable costs and lower upfront costs (pay-as-you-go, no large capital outlay). The other options misstate the cost model.

questions.question: Which AWS service would a customer use with a static website to achieve tower latency and high transfer speeds?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront delivers a static website with lower latency and high transfer speeds by caching at edge locations. Lambda is compute, DAX accelerates DynamoDB, and Route 53 is DNS.

questions.question: How do Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups help achieve high availability for a web application?

options.text: They automatically add more instances across multiple AWS Regions based on global demand of the application.
They automatically add or replace instances across multiple Availability Zones when the application needs it.
They enable the application’s stalk: content to reside closer to end users.
They are able to distribute incoming requests across a tier of web server instances.

questions.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling groups achieve high availability by automatically adding or replacing instances across multiple Availability Zones as needed. They do not span Regions automatically, cache content, or load-balance traffic (that is ELB).

questions.question: Which of the following can limit Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket access to specific users?

options.text: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies.

questions.explanation: IAM policies limit S3 bucket access to specific users. Key pairs, Inspector, and security groups do not control per-user bucket access.

questions.question: How should a customer forecast the future costs for running a new web application?
questions.explanation: The AWS Simple Monthly Calculator forecasts the future cost of a new application's services. (Note: it has been replaced by the AWS Pricing Calculator.) Aurora Backtrack, CloudWatch billing alarms, and the Cost & Usage Report do not forecast new-app costs.

questions.question: Where are AWS compliance documents, such as an SOC 1 report, located?
questions.explanation: AWS compliance documents such as SOC 1 reports are available in AWS Artifact. Inspector scans, CloudTrail logs, and Certificate Manager handles certificates.

questions.question: Which of the following tasks is the responsibility of AWS?

options.text: Configuring AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles.

questions.explanation: Securing the Amazon EC2 hypervisor is AWS's responsibility (security of the cloud). Client-side encryption, IAM role configuration, and password policies are customer responsibilities.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model which of the following areas are the customer’s responsibility? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for patching their operating systems (B) and configuring security groups (E). Network firmware upgrades, hypervisor patching, and physical data-center security are AWS responsibilities.

questions.question: A company is looking for a scalable data warehouse solution. Which of the following AWS solutions would meet the company’s needs?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is AWS's scalable data warehouse solution. S3 is object storage, DynamoDB is NoSQL, and Kinesis processes streaming data.

questions.question: Which AWS services provide a way to extend an on-premises architecture to the AWS Cloud? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect (B) and AWS Storage Gateway (D) extend an on-premises architecture into AWS (dedicated connectivity and hybrid storage). EBS, CloudFront, and Connect do not.

questions.question: What are the advantages of the AWS Cloud (Select TWO)

options.text: No need to guess capacity requirements.
Physical access to cloud data centers.

questions.explanation: AWS Cloud advantages include no need to guess capacity requirements (B) and increased speed to market (C). AWS lowers (not increases) upfront capital expenditure, costs are variable (not fixed monthly), and you do not get physical data-center access.

questions.question: How can the AWS Cloud increase user workforce productivity after migration from an on-premises data center?

options.text: Users do not have to wait for infrastructure provisioning.
The AWS Cloud infrastructure is much faster than an on-premises data center infrastructure.
AWS takes over application configuration management on behalf of users.
Users do not need to address security and compliance issues.

questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud increases productivity because users no longer wait for infrastructure to be provisioned — resources are available in minutes. AWS does not take over your configuration management or remove your security/compliance duties.

questions.question: Which of the following services could be used to deploy an application to servers running on-premises? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS OpsWorks (B) and AWS CodeDeploy (C) can deploy applications to on-premises servers as well as AWS. Elastic Beanstalk, Batch, and X-Ray do not deploy to on-premises servers.

questions.question: What is an example of agility in the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Using Consolidated Billing to produce one bill.
Decreased acquisition time for new compute resources.

questions.explanation: Agility in AWS is shown by the decreased acquisition time for new compute resources (minutes instead of weeks). Instance variety, managed services, and consolidated billing illustrate other benefits.

questions.question: Which AWS security service protects applications from distributed denial of service attacks with always-on detection and automatic inline mitigations?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield protects applications from DDoS attacks with always-on detection and automatic inline mitigation. Inspector scans, WAF filters web requests, and ELB distributes traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of AWS consolidated billing? (Choose two)

options.text: The ability to receive one bill for multiple accounts.
Service limits increasing by default in all accounts.
A fixed discount on the monthly bill.
Potential volume discounts, as usage in all accounts is combined.
The automatic extension of the master account’s AWS support plan to all accounts.

questions.explanation: Consolidated billing advantages include receiving one bill for multiple accounts (A) and potential volume discounts from combined usage (D). It does not raise service limits by default, give a fixed discount, or extend the support plan to all accounts.

questions.question: A company is considering using AWS for a self-hosted database that requires a nightly shutdown for maintenance and cost-saving purposes. Which service should the company use?

options.text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) with Amazon EC2 instance store.
Amazon EC2 with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).

questions.explanation: For a self-hosted database needing nightly shutdowns, use Amazon EC2 with Amazon EBS, because EBS persists data across stop/start (saving cost while stopped). Instance store loses data on stop, and Redshift/DynamoDB are managed services.
